why: The pilot's thesis from log 002 (2026-10-20): a wheel is a finisher dropped onto Brallin or Shabraz, never early tempo, and the deck runs too many of them. The champion, flown by his policy (hold every wheel until a commander is out), reads 0.797 on finisher wheel by T8; 0.82 is the nearest line the grading run can resolve. THE OBJECTIVE IS A GUARD, NOT THE VERDICT. The pre-registered profile, judged as a whole table and then at his table: dead wheels in hand @T5 DOWN; kept hand passes the pilot's keep rule UP; hand can act by T3 up or flat; both commanders out by T6 flat or up; extra cards by T8 and killed by T10 must not fall by more than their MDE; stall flat; wheels cast by T10 reported with no direction. Candidates come slot by slot with the pilot: of the eighteen wheel-shaped cards, the ones that also DO something and the repeatables on bodies hold their value, a bare seven-for-seven only Shabraz pays is the first to question; freed slots go to bodies, ramp or cheap draw. Torbran and Marauding Mako are keeps. Damage by turn X is not the question.

summary.title: Wheels as the finish, not the opening
summary.blurb: After game two at Oliver's: too many wheels, fired too early. Eleven swaps by argument: the wheel-shaped cards go from eighteen to nine, the ones that pay both commanders stay, and four rocks, five bodies that cash a wheel and one-mana protection come in. Read at the table, by slices and by Forge counts.

staged.why: a five-mana refill that pays Shabraz only, for red-blue ramp that survives Araumi's edicts (the strategist: the template gap is ramp; the keep slice: rocks land the commanders)
one mana, random, symmetrical and always on turn two — the early wheel the pilot called wrong (log 002); for red-white ramp
a fragile repeatable early wheel for blue-red ramp
five mana before it draws anything, for ramp plus no maximum hand size on the seven you just drew
a six-drop that wheels on every spell (churn, not a finish) for a two-mana flyer that connives on anyone's second spell
the third copy of Windfall's job for a body that grows on your discards and makes Treasure off a discarded land
ten mana for the full card, interaction already covered, for instant red removal, a loot or a Treasure
tier two (wheel density 13 -> 9): a two-mana early-tempo wheel for a two-mana flying haste body that gets +2/+0 per card discarded — the wheel's payoff on a red body for Torbran
tier two: a shuffle wheel that pays only Shabraz unless metalcraft is on, for a two-mana flyer that takes a counter per card discarded and cycles when the hand has no play

tier two: the whole table discards and redraws every upkeep — the political cost the pilot named (log 002) as a permanent — for a two-mana flyer that makes a flyer on the second draw each turn, which every wheel is
tier two: a two-card mini-wheel that is mostly ramp (the rocks now carry that) for one-mana hexproof and indestructible on the commander the wheel is waiting on
